presentingComplaint: 2 days of mild exertional breathlessness and vague upper-abdominal/lower-chest heaviness, now settling at rest
history: Retired schoolteacher with type 2 diabetes (18 years, on metformin + gliclazide), hypertension and dyslipidaemia. Over the last 48 hours she noticed she had to stop twice while walking to the temple because of a dull, heavy discomfort across the lower chest and epigastrium, associated with breathlessness and mild sweating. She attributed it to 'gas/acidity' and took an antacid with partial relief. No severe crushing pain, no radiation she can clearly describe, no collapse. Episodes last 10-15 minutes and ease with rest. Two brief similar episodes overnight woke her. She remains largely well between episodes. Ex-smoker (quit 10 years ago), father had MI at 60. Diabetic autonomic neuropathy suspected on prior review.
examination: Comfortable at rest, not distressed. Chest clear, no crepitations, normal heart sounds, no murmur or added sounds. JVP not raised, no peripheral oedema. Abdomen soft, mild epigastric tenderness only, no guarding. Peripheral pulses intact and symmetric; equal BP in both arms. No calf swelling.
imaging: Chest X-ray: no consolidation, no pulmonary oedema, normal cardiac silhouette, no widened mediastinum. Bedside echo: mild regional hypokinesia of the inferolateral wall, preserved overall LV function (EF ~52%), no pericardial effusion, no RV strain.
differentialDiagnoses: NSTEMI / non-ST-elevation ACS (inferolateral territory) - fits dynamic troponin, subtle ECG changes and regional wall-motion abnormality
GORD / acid-peptic disease - suggested by epigastric heaviness and antacid response, but does not explain rising troponin
Pericarditis - excluded by absence of pleuritic positional pain, rub and typical diffuse ST changes
Pulmonary embolism - possible with dyspnoea but no RV strain, normal SpO2/A-a and no leg findings
Acute decompensated heart failure - mildly raised NT-proBNP but no congestion clinically or radiographically
finalDiagnosis: Non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTEMI) presenting atypically as anginal-equivalent dyspnoea and epigastric discomfort in an elderly diabetic woman
citations: ESC Guidelines for the Management of Acute Coronary Syndromes 2023
ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Non-ST-Elevation ACS 2014
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e - Non-ST-Segment Elevation Acute Coronary Syndrome
stewardship: Not applicable - non-infective condition; no antimicrobial therapy indicated.
contraindications: Avoid nitrates if inferior/RV involvement with hypotension or recent PDE5 inhibitor use
Caution with high-dose beta-blockade if signs of low output or bradyarrhythmia
Metformin held around planned coronary angiography given contrast and eGFR
edgeCases: Diabetic autonomic neuropathy blunts classic pain, so anginal-equivalent (dyspnoea, epigastric heaviness) is the dominant symptom
Elderly women more often present with atypical/mild ACS and are under-triaged
Single normal first troponin is insufficient; the diagnosis rests on the significant delta on serial high-sensitivity troponin
expectedMaiK: In an elderly diabetic with anginal-equivalent dyspnoea/epigastric discomfort, a significant rise in serial high-sensitivity troponin with a regional wall-motion abnormality confirms NSTEMI even when pain is mild and ECG changes are subtle.
expectedNextQuestions: Are the episodes clearly provoked by exertion and relieved by rest (crescendo pattern)?
Any prior stress test, angiogram or known coronary disease?
Any bleeding risk factors before dual antiplatelet therapy and anticoagulation?
GRACE risk features: ongoing symptoms, haemodynamic or rhythm instability?
expectedInvestigations: 12-lead ECG immediately and repeated / continuous ST monitoring
Transthoracic echocardiogram for regional wall motion and LV function
Coronary angiography (early invasive strategy for intermediate-high risk NSTE-ACS)
regressionAssertions: acs must be the top diagnosis despite atypical/mild presentation
A significant delta on serial hs-troponin must drive the diagnosis over a single value
gerd_chest must not be selected as final diagnosis despite epigastric symptoms and antacid response
